products.name: Zscaler AI
products.note: Cloud security AI; SSE platform; data loss prevention; AI traffic inspection

reading.body:
Zscaler sells AI-powered security tools for cloud infrastructure, positioning data inspection and governance of AI agent interactions as competitive priorities for enterprises.

Zscaler's product focus reflects a real constraint in AI deployment: as models handle sensitive data at scale, the security layer becomes inseparable from the compute layer. The company's emphasis on "agent-to-agent interactions" and data lineage tracing suggests enterprise customers are already grappling with governance challenges that arise when multiple AI systems operate in the same environment. This is not a future problem. It is operational now.

The data does not specify what fraction of Zscaler's revenue comes from AI-specific capabilities versus traditional cloud security, or how the Zero Trust Exchange infrastructure itself scales with AI workloads. It also does not cover whether Zscaler's own systems are bottlenecks for customers trying to inspect high-velocity AI traffic in real time. Security-as-a-service sits between compute and the data it processes, which means architectural choices here can either enable or constrain AI scaling.

Zscaler's headquarters in California and 175 cases of legal exposure in that state suggest ongoing regulatory or compliance friction, though the specific nature of those cases is not detailed. For a company selling governance tools to AI operators, regulatory clarity in its own jurisdiction may correlate with its ability to help customers navigate the same uncertainty elsewhere.

profile_text.body:
Zscaler describes itself as a leading cloud enterprise security provider helping global businesses adopt zero trust for secure digital transformation. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in San Jose, California, it is a public company traded on NASDAQ under ticker ZS. Its unified cybersecurity platform is built on what the company calls the Zero Trust Exchange, which it says sits inline on every connection and connects each entity only to what it is authorized to reach so the attack surface disappears. The company states the same platform secures users, data, AI agents, and AI models, and helps security operations centers stop threats at machine speed.

The company's site lists capabilities including AI Asset Management, AI Security, Attack Surface Management, BYOD Security, Continuous Threat Exposure Management, Data Security, Microsegmentation, OT Segmentation, VPN replacement, Secure Access to AI, Secure B2B, Secure East-West Traffic, Secure Ingress and Egress Traffic, Secure IoT/OT, Secure the Workforce, Security Context Graph, Zero Trust + AI, and Zero Trust SD-WAN. Zscaler AI is described as cloud security AI covering an SSE platform, data loss prevention, and AI traffic inspection. The company notes analyst recognition from Gartner, Forrester, and others, and operates Zenith Ventures, which it says invests in zero trust and AI startups.

Public records list 281 legal matters in California involving Zscaler. The company's site also points to compliance certifications, corporate responsibility, investor relations with SEC filings, and a leadership team.
